release_gate: Hosted QA green; main merge and stable publication require Matthew's explicit approval.

user_issues.selection: Typed application causes and optical IssueKind values; diagnostic prose never selects guidance.
user_issues.presentation: Localized plain-language cause and next action, with evidence-backed firmware consequences.
user_issues.before_write: A blocked update states that no firmware was written, including after a backup was saved.
user_issues.after_entry: Distinguish attempted update entry from firmware payload transfer; never claim no change after uncertain writes.
user_issues.read_only: Read-only capabilities explicitly establish that the operation did not write firmware.
user_issues.unknown: Unexpected faults retain diagnostics and ask for a diagnostic report; no guessed cause or retry advice.
user_issues.reports: Keep the stable issue ID, arguments and consequences alongside the full technical chain.

firmware_lifecycle.provided_current: Reject known incompatible families offline before opening a drive; missing evidence cannot establish compatibility.
firmware_lifecycle.live_current: Finish acquisition, publish and read back the required normal-flash backup, then perform family admission.
firmware_lifecycle.acquisition: Acquire once; a second full read is permitted only for intentional stability verification.
firmware_lifecycle.consent: Keep the actual owned prepared recovery update through confirmation. Confirmation does not reopen input files or reacquire the installed firmware.
firmware_lifecycle.execution: Consume the prepared session once; lightweight receiver revalidation precedes the engine-owned write grant and library execution checks.
firmware_lifecycle.verification: Postwrite target identity and independent component readback remain mandatory.
firmware_lifecycle.recovery: No automatic backup. Known supplied-file family mismatches are refused unless an explicit override is supported and requested. Pioneer retains its installed-family gate by default. MediaTek receivers without installed-family evidence retain the library's recovery admission policy. Receiver, integrity and chip checks still apply.

progress.measured: Show observed completed bytes against known total bytes.
progress.waiting: Show indeterminate restart/wait status without inventing percentages.
progress.expected_responses: Restart-related transport responses remain diagnostic evidence, with completion decided by independent verification.

architecture.application: CLI, GUI and workflow consume generic prepared updates, structured user issues and phase events.
architecture.adapters: Translate optical library types to generic application contracts.
architecture.optical_libraries: Own protocol sequencing, receiver preparation, execution and verification; mirror operation enums, progress structure and CodedError::kind across both packages.
architecture.candidate_dependencies: Exact 1.1.0 versions and immutable 40-character git revisions; no machine-local paths.

required_validation: All 29 catalogs contain every user-issue and phase key
Known mock update failures cannot fall through to the unexpected-error message
Packaging and offline command failures prove no firmware write; known verification and option refusals retain their cause
A lost worker or native event loop preserves active write uncertainty, while read-only tasks prove no firmware write
Unsafe write evidence overrides every file or compatibility cause
Supplied cross-family Current rejects before opening an invalid device selector
Prepared recovery executes once without repeating acquisition and rejects a changed receiver
GUI confirmation carries the prepared handle and cancellation drops it
Both optical libraries exercise measured writes, restart waits and independent verification
Both optical libraries pass their feature matrix, MSRV, documentation, packaging and no-std gates
Application workspace tests, lint, release tests, native GUI gates and release packaging pass on hosted QA
hardware: No new hardware writes are authorized by this goal. Hosted QA cannot prove physical-drive behavior.
